text:
sarah-sales: Heads up — ACME demo is seeing repeated 503s during our hands-on. Customer hit a 30min window where ~40% of requests failed. They want a post-mortem and a quick mitigation so the POC stays healthy.
sarah-sales: Symptoms: spikes at ~2k rps, latencies climb then 5xxs. They mentioned sudden ramp from their side during conversation.
tyler-support: Sorry — jumping in. Can you paste a sample request ID or a time window? I’ll pull recent request logs.
sarah-sales: Here’s one request id from their dashboard: req_f1a9b2c3, happened at 2026-03-20T15:12:07Z.
tyler-support: Got it. I’m running a quick query now.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] new autoscaler event: scale-up-request queued at 2026-03-20T15:12:10Z -> delay observed: 18s.
maria-eng: Seeing the logs for req_f1a9b2c3 — downstream inference node returned 502 -> gateway turned into 503 after retries. Stack traces show OOMs on one pod and backpressure on the router:
```
2026-03-20T15:12:07Z req_f1a9b2c3 TRACE kernel: kvcache miss
2026-03-20T15:12:09Z node-42 ERROR inference: out-of-memory (alloc failed)
2026-03-20T15:12:09Z router WARN overcommit: queue-depth=24 > threshold=20
```
maria-eng: Looks like autoscaler triggered but the new instances were slow to register (GC + image pull on their dedicated pool). That explains the ~15–25s window where router backlog grew and frontend returned 503s.
alex-ml: Noting this was a demo with long-context prompts (3k tokens). That bumps mem usage. We can suggest a memory-safe model variant or reduce context for demo. Also can enable kv-cache warmup to reduce cold allocation.
josh-sre: For near-term mitigation: 1) gate the customer’s concurrency via a temporary rate-limit rule (reduce to 60% of current) 2) add a short-term reserved instance (= one N4 node) for this customer’s pool 3) change fallback policy to use a smaller model variant until full capacity registers. Which option does sales prefer for fast action?
sarah-sales: They want minimal friction. Reserved node might need procurement. Can we do rate-limit + fallback model immediately?
maria-eng: Yes — I can push a routing policy change to route their requests to model-lt-quant (lower mem) as a fallback. That should reduce OOMs. I’ll also enable faster image pre-pull on the affected pool to reduce node join latency.
tyler-support: I’ll add a short-lived quota: customer_acme_demo -> concurrency: 120 -> effective immediately. Also adding a diagnostic flag to increase logging for 5xx correlation ids for 1 hour.
sarah-sales: Thanks. Can you confirm ETA for the routing change? I have the customer on the call.
maria-eng: Routing change applied in 30s.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] routing-policy update: customer_acme_demo fallback=model-lt-quant applied by maria-eng at 2026-03-20T15:14:02Z.
kevin-demo: Confirmed with ACME — errors dropped almost instantly. They still see 100–200ms extra latency on fallback but no 5xx. They’re happy for now.
josh-sre: Follow-ups: 1) we should run an autoscale tuning job for that pool to reduce cold-join latency (pre-pull + smaller image + GC flags) 2) add an alert if router queue_depth > 15 for >30s 3) review billing/quotas for demo bursts so sales can offer predictable options. I’ll create tasks.
maria-eng: I opened ENG-5421 for autoscale tuning and ENG-5422 for pre-pull job.
tyler-support: I’ll collect the expanded log bundle and upload to the deal thread. Request IDs included: req_f1a9b2c3, req_a7b4c9d2, req_f9c0e3b1.
sarah-sales: Closing loop: ACME said this workaround is acceptable for demo. They asked for a short write-up on root cause and permanent fixes (autoscale tuning + model suggestion). Can you draft an internal summary I can forward to them?
josh-sre: I’ll draft the post-mortem and tag you. Short summary: rapid customer ramp + large-context prompts -> node OOMs -> delayed autoscale join -> router queue overflow -> 503s. Temporary mitigation: concurrency cap + fallback model + pre-pull. Long-term: autoscaler tuning and reserved capacity option for enterprise POCs.
sarah-sales: Perfect. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
kevin-demo: +1 — will keep monitoring for the next 24h and update if anything else pops up.
